script.title: Why Admirers Took Galileo's Middle Finger From His Grave
sentences: Galileo's middle finger sits inside a gilded glass egg in Florence.
When the astronomer died in 1642, authorities barred him from consecrated ground.
Ninety-five years later, his remains were moved inside the Basilica di Santa Croce.
During the transfer, three men took three fingers, a tooth, and a vertebra.
Two fingers vanished after 1905, resurfacing at auction in 2009.
The middle finger was even mislabeled as a left index finger.
Yet admirers treated the heretic like a saint, preserving the finger that mapped unseen skies.
Today it sits at the Museo Galileo, right beside his telescope lens.

Today the Museo Galileo displays it inside a gilded glass egg beside his telescope lens.

claims_en: Galileo's middle finger is encased in a gilded glass egg in Florence.
Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei died in 1642.
Authorities from the Catholic Church did not want Galileo buried on consecrated grounds.
Ninety-five years after his death, in 1737, Galileo's remains were transferred to a mausoleum inside the Basilica di Santa Croce in Florence.
During the transfer, three men removed three fingers (the middle finger, index finger, and thumb), a tooth, and a vertebra.
Galileo's thumb and index finger disappeared after 1905 and turned up at auction in 2009.
The middle finger was originally listed in the museum's inventory as Galileo's left index finger.
Admirers treated Galileo, whose remains came from a heretic's grave, like a saint, preserving his finger as a secular relic for pointing out unseen worlds in the sky.
Galileo's middle finger is displayed at the Museo Galileo alongside the objective lens from his telescope.
